edition.en: The complete essay, including Thoreau’s poem “The Old Marlborough Road”, from Project Gutenberg eBook #1022. Verse quoted inside the prose is run on with slashes. The Greek line Thoreau quotes from the Chaldean Oracles, lost in that e-text, is restored, and four readings (among them “howling mother of ours” for “hovering”) are corrected where the 1862 Atlantic text and the Excursions printing agree.
edition.zh: 全文，包括梭罗自己的诗《老马尔伯勒路》，据古登堡计划电子书 1022。文中引用的诗句以斜线连排。梭罗所引《迦勒底神谕》的那行希腊文在该电子本中已经损坏，现予恢复；另有四处异文（包括把 howling mother of ours 误作 hovering），凡 1862 年《大西洋月刊》文本与《远足集》印本一致之处，均已改正。

basis.en: Published in The Atlantic Monthly in 1862; Henry David Thoreau died in 1862.
basis.zh: 1862 年刊于《大西洋月刊》；梭罗卒于 1862 年。

note.en: Thoreau’s essay, printed in The Atlantic Monthly in 1862, begins as a defence of sauntering and widens into a case for wildness as something people need, not merely tolerate. It has his best jokes about the word “saunterer” and his own small poem about a road nobody repairs. The closing pages describe a November sunset over a meadow that, he imagines, will “cheer and reassure the latest child that walked there”. The Chinese translates the whole essay, the poem included.
note.zh: 梭罗的这篇文章 1862 年刊于《大西洋月刊》，从为“闲逛”辩护开始，渐渐扩展为一种主张：野性是人所需要的，而不只是可以容忍的。文中有他拿“闲逛者”一词开的最好的玩笑，还有他写一条无人修补的路的小诗。结尾几页写十一月草地上的一次落日，他想象那光会“鼓舞、安慰将来最后一个走在那里的孩子”。中文译出全文，包括那首诗。

excerpt.orig: So we saunter toward the Holy Land, till one day the sun shall shine more brightly than ever he has done
excerpt.en: So we saunter toward the Holy Land, till one day the sun shall shine more brightly than ever he has done
excerpt.zh: 我们就这样向着圣地闲逛而去，直到有一天，太阳照得比以往任何时候都更明亮

gloss.en: A preacher of the First Crusade (1096), said to have stirred crowds across France to march for Jerusalem.
gloss.zh: 第一次十字军东征（1096）的布道者，据说曾在法国各地鼓动民众向耶路撒冷进发。

gloss.en: Latin: “The walker is born, not made”, after the proverb Poeta nascitur, non fit, “the poet is born, not made”.
gloss.zh: 拉丁文：“步行者是天生的，不是造就的。”仿自谚语 Poeta nascitur, non fit（诗人是天生的，不是造就的）。

gloss.en: Dahomey was a West African kingdom, in present-day Benin, much described by nineteenth-century travellers.
gloss.zh: 达荷美是西非的一个王国，在今贝宁境内，19 世纪的游记中常有描述。

gloss.en: Manu, the lawgiver of Hindu tradition, to whom the Laws of Manu are ascribed.
gloss.zh: 摩奴，印度传统中的立法者，《摩奴法典》托名于他。

gloss.en: Lethe, the river of forgetfulness in the Greek underworld; whoever drank from it forgot their former life.
gloss.zh: 忘川，希腊神话中冥界的遗忘之河，饮其水者忘却前生。

gloss.en: In Greek myth, the nymphs who kept a garden of golden apples at the western edge of the world.
gloss.zh: 希腊神话中在世界西端看守金苹果园的仙女。

gloss.en: In Greek legend, the founder of Thebes, said to have brought the alphabet to Greece from Phoenicia.
gloss.zh: 希腊传说中忒拜城的建立者，相传把字母从腓尼基带到了希腊。
